parent_context.title: fix: route torch to a CUDA index on aarch64 (DGX Spark / GB10)
parent_context.text:
## Problem

Every `train` command dies on a DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64) before iteration 0:

```
File "mjlab/utils/gpu.py", line 70, in select_gpus
  selected_gpus = [available_gpus[i] for i in gpu_ids]
IndexError: list index out of range
```

## Root cause

Nothing was wrong with the GPU — warp saw `cuda:0` (sm_121, 122 GiB) the whole
time. Only torch was blind.

On linux-aarch64, PyPI's torch wheel is **CPU-only**: `torch.__version__` is
`2.9.1+cpu` and `torch.version.cuda` is `None`. So `torch.cuda.device_count()`
returns 0, `select_gpus()` builds an empty `available_gpus`, and indexing it
raises. The traceback points at GPU *selection*, which sends you looking at
drivers and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; the actual fault is which wheel got
installed.

## Fix

Route torch to PyTorch's cu129 index, scoped by marker to aarch64 only.

**cu129 rather than cu130** because it matches the CUDA toolkit warp 1.12.0
bundles (warp reports "CUDA Toolkit 12.9"), keeping mjlab's zero-copy
warp↔torch interop on one runtime major version.

Two details this depends on. Both are silent when broken — `uv sync` succeeds
and you only find out at launch:

1. **torch must be a DIRECT dependency.** uv applies `[tool.uv.sources]` to
   direct deps only, so while torch arrived purely via mjlab/rsl_rl the index
   was ignored with no warning. The `torch==` line looks redundant; it isn't.
2. **The pin must be `==`, not `>=`.** The CUDA index carries newer builds than
   the PyPI pin, so `torch>=2.7.0` pulled 2.9.1 → 2.13.0 (and torchvision →
   0.28.0). `==2.9.1` changes only the wheel's source, not its version.

## HF Jobs are unaffected

Verified, not assumed. Evaluating every package's `resolution-markers` against
an x86_64-linux env and diffing `develop` vs this branch:

```
packages resolving on x86_64-linux:  develop=142  branch=142
  added: (none)   removed: (none)   changed: (none)
torch on x86 -> [('2.9.1', 'https://pypi.org/simple')]
x86 packages sourced from the CUDA index: (none)
```

Identical package for package. All three HF flavors (`l4x1`, `a10g-large`,
`a100-large`) are x86_64, `uv lock --check` passes so the container resolves
straight from the lock without re-resolving, and the persistent uv cache stays
warm.

The large `uv.lock` diff is mostly uv annotating explicit `version`/`source` on
transitive packages now that two resolution branches exist. The real change is
the torch entry splitting in two:

| resolution-markers | source | version |
|---|---|---|
| `platform_machine != 'aarch64' or sys_platform != 'linux'` | pypi.org | `2.9.1` |
| `platform_machine == 'aarch64' and sys_platform == 'linux'` | download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129 | `2.9.1+cu129` |

## Regression guards

`tests/test_aarch64_cuda_torch.py` locks both silent failure modes plus the
x86_64 side. Five tests parse `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock` and run anywhere (CPU,
no GPU); the sixth self-skips unless on ARM with a working `nvidia-smi`, where
it asserts `torch.cuda.device_count() > 0` — a direct reproduction of the crash.

The guards were verified to **fail against the pre-fix `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`**,
not merely to pass here.

## Test plan

Run on the DGX Spark from a **deleted `.venv`**, to exercise the clean-clone
path that originally failed:

- [x] fresh `uv sync` → 142 packages
- [x] torch `2.9.1+cu129`, cuda 12.9, 1 device, 4096² GPU matmul
- [x] `pytest tests/` → **155 passed**
- [x] smoke test (64 envs / 5 iters) → `device=cuda:0`, `nan_state: 0.0000`
- [x] **the original failing command** (4096 envs, 20 iters) → ~2.67 s/iter,
      reward 2.06 → 2.36, no NaN
- [x] ONNX export from checkpoint → input `obs [1, 61]`, output `actions [1, 14]`,
      finite (61D actor obs invariant holds)

## Notes for reviewers

torch prints a startup warning on GB10, and it is expected:

```
Found GPU0 NVIDIA GB10 which is of cuda capability 12.1.
Minimum and Maximum cuda capability supported by this version of PyTorch is (8.0) - (12.0)
```

torch 2.9.1's arch list tops out at `sm_120`; GB10 is `sm_121`, and sm_120
cubins are family-compatible — confirmed by real matmuls and full 4096-env
training steps. When bumping torch, prefer a release with native sm_121. If a
`no kernel image is available` error ever appears, switching the index URL to
`cu130` provides `compute_120` PTX JIT fallback (that build was tested working
on this GPU too).

No CI workflow is included (deliberate — repo has none today), so the guards
run only when someone runs pytest. No `src/` changes: RL training behavior is
byte-identical.

text:
## Throughput benchmark on DGX Spark (GB10)

Numbers for this branch on the target hardware. Before the fix there is nothing
to compare against — `train` crashed in `select_gpus()` before iteration 0, so
throughput was effectively zero on this machine.

**Setup**: `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, torch `2.9.1+cu129`, warp 1.12.0
(CUDA 12.9), driver 580.173.02, NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121, aarch64), 25 iterations per
config with the first 5 discarded as warmup (warp kernel load + cache).
`env-steps/s = num_envs × 24 / iter_time` (`NUM_STEPS_PER_ENV = 24`).

| envs | iter time | env-steps/s | 4000 iters (est.) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 0.860 s | 14,288 | 0.96 h |
| 1024 | 1.018 s | 24,153 | 1.13 h |
| 2048 | 1.464 s | 33,585 | 1.63 h |
| **4096** | **2.672 s** | **36,784** | **2.97 h** |
| 8192 | 6.535 s | 30,085 | 7.26 h |
| 16384 | 19.782 s | 19,877 | 21.98 h |

Timings are highly reproducible — steady-state standard deviation is 0.008 s at
4096, 0.022 s at 8192, 0.015 s at 16384. Only iteration 1 shows warmup cost.
Every config ran on `device=cuda:0` with `nan_state: 0.0000` and no errors.

### Findings

**4096 envs is the throughput sweet spot** at ~36.8k env-steps/s, which is
already the default in the README. Past that it degrades rather than plateaus:
8192 gives 18% *fewer* steps/s than 4096, and 16384 gives 46% fewer. 16384 costs
3.0× the per-iteration time of 8192 for 2× the envs, which looks like GB10's
unified memory becoming the bottleneck. There is no reason to raise `--num-envs`
above 4096 on this box.

Scaling is only strong up to ~2048 (512 → 2048 gains 2.35× throughput for 4×
the envs); 2048 → 4096 gains just 9%.

### Caveat on wall-clock estimates

The last column is `iter_time × 4000` and assumes constant per-iteration cost —
it is arithmetic, not a measured full run. CLAUDE.md budgets gaits at 4000–6000
iterations, so a full walking run at 4096 envs lands around **3–4.5 h** here.
That sits above the README's "~1–2 h for a usable gait at 4096 envs", which was
presumably measured on a faster x86 GPU (or counts "usable" well before 4000
iterations). Worth a follow-up to reconcile, but out of scope for this PR — I
have not trained a gait to completion on this hardware to check.

parent_context.title: Add play-dead task: stand, flop onto the back, and hold
parent_context.text:
## Why

Sit is a polite sit. Roulade lands on its feet. Standup starts already down. Nothing in the pad means **die and stay dead** — swap the ONNX in, the duck goes down and holds; swap sitstand/standup to revive.

Play-dead is **supine** (belly up, −90° pitch), not “inverted”. `upright_cos = −1` is a headstand **and** a face-plant; a policy will farm whichever is cheaper. The orientation signal is world-z of body +X (`body_supine_cos_from_quat`). Height rewards are gated on `supine_cos > 0` so sitting (`z ≈ 0.060`) cannot collect the dead-height peak.

## What

- New env family `Mjlab-PlayDead-{Flat,Rough}-MicroDuck` (+ backlash twins on the allcollisions model)
- 61D actor obs: 48 proprio + twist(3) + head(4) pad + body(6) pad — hot-swappable with walk/stand/roulade
- Reset mix: 75% standing (learn the flop) / 25% already face-up (learn the hold); reverse curriculum raises the dead fraction; face-down stays at 0
- `scripts/infer_policy.py --playdead` (key **D**). Default is hold-until-D-again — play-dead does not end standing
- CPU cfg tests lock the contract, signs, sit-basin audit, and registration

## AGENTS.md bar

```bash
uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_playdead_cfg.py
uv run train Mjlab-PlayDead-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5
```

Ran on a Spark (GB10): 16 play-dead tests + full CPU suite (171) green. Smoke 64 envs × 5 iters: actor obs **(61,)**, every reward term computed, `Episode_Termination/nan_state = 0`, self-negating penalties logged **≤ 0**, ONNX export **61 → 14**.

This is the env, not a converged policy. A real run is `~1000–2000` iters at 4096 envs (`experiment_name=microduck_playdead`), then `scripts/export.py` (bakes the normalizer — mandatory).

## Deploy rehearsal

```bash
uv run scripts/infer_policy.py --walking walk.onnx --standing stand.onnx \
    --playdead playdead.onnx --new-cmd-obs
```

`D` plays dead and holds; `D` again hands back. Revive with standup/sitstand, not walk.

parent_context.title: Add 16-DOF footed Growbot Roulade simulation
parent_context.text:
## Summary

- add a dedicated 16-actuator footed Growbot asset derived from the Microduck collision model
- bind the custom Growbot head, compact arms, and three-finger hand meshes while retaining lightweight collision hulls
- add one actuated elbow pitch joint per arm and extend bilateral symmetry to 14- and 16-joint policies
- register `Mjlab-Growbot-Roulade-Flat` with separate 67D actor, 80D critic, and 16D action contracts
- preserve all existing Microduck tasks and checkpoint dimensions

## Validation

- `165 passed, 1 skipped`
- five-iteration CUDA smoke run with 64 environments and 7,680 steps
- approximately 2,465 simulation steps/second on an RTX 3070
- zero NaN terminations
- checkpoint and ONNX export produced successfully
- 200-frame, 960x720 evaluation recording produced successfully

## Notes

The long Roulade training run is intentionally not included. This PR establishes and validates the corrected simulation asset and policy contract before committing GPU time to convergence training.

parent_context.title: Add AMD GPU (ROCm/HIP) training support
parent_context.text:
## Add AMD GPU (ROCm/HIP) training support

microduck_rl trains through mjlab -> mujoco-warp -> NVIDIA Warp, a CUDA-only
stack, so it does not run on AMD GPUs out of the box (`torch.cuda.is_available()`
is False and training crashes in `select_gpus()` with 0 CUDA devices). This PR
adds a self-contained `rocm/` directory that runs the same training on **AMD
Instinct GPUs** via AMD's ROCm/HIP port of Warp, with **no changes to the
physics, task, or training code** (the invariants in `AGENTS.md` are untouched).

### Verified

On an **MI300X (gfx942), ROCm 10.0**, from a fresh clone of this branch:

- `rocm/setup_rocm.sh` builds the ROCm Warp wheel, installs a HIP-matched ROCm
  PyTorch, and applies the dependency patches: exit 0.
- `rocm/verify_rocm.sh`: torch and Warp both see the GPU and coexist in one
  process (`BOTH_OK`).
- `rocm/train_rocm.sh Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 4096`:
  trains to exit 0, mean reward increasing, with `rocm-smi` showing **100% GPU
  utilization and multi-GB VRAM sustained** through the run (idle the instant it
  ends), confirming physics and the PPO update run on the GPU, not a CPU
  fallback.

### What it does

The enabling piece is [AMD-Ecosystem/warp](https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/warp)
(branch `amd-integration`), a ROCm/HIP build of Warp. Given that Warp build plus
a HIP-major-matched PyTorch, four small dependency incompatibilities remain,
fixed idempotently by `rocm/patch_rocm.py`:

| # | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---------|-----|
| 1 | stream create fails / `version 'hip_7.1' not found` | HIP-major-7 torch + `LD_PRELOAD` of system ROCm hip/hsa/hiprtc so torch and Warp share one HIP runtime (handled by the launcher) |
| 2 | `module 'warp' has no attribute 'context'` | `.pth` + shim aliasing `warp.context` -> `warp._src.context` |
| 3 | `Conditional graph nodes are not supported on HIP/ROCm` | set `opt.graph_conditional = False` so the solver uses its native Python-loop branch |
| 4 | `Failed to create CUDA texture ... error 801` | guard mujoco-warp's texture creation with its existing `use_textures` flag |

Fixes 2 to 4 live in installed dependencies (`warp`, `mjlab`, `mujoco_warp`), so
they are applied by a re-runnable post-install patcher (`--check` mode included)
rather than as edits to this repo's source.

### Files (all additive, under `rocm/`)

- `rocm/setup_rocm.sh` - build ROCm Warp for the local GPU arch, install ROCm
  torch, apply patches (autodetects `ROCM_PATH` / arch; env-overridable).
- `rocm/patch_rocm.py` - idempotent dependency patcher, `--check` reports status.
- `rocm/train_rocm.sh` - launcher that sets `LD_PRELOAD`, then `uv run train "$@"`.
- `rocm/verify_rocm.sh` - proves torch + Warp coexist on the GPU.
- `rocm/README.md` - approach, version matrix, and limitations.
- one pointer line added to the main `README.md`.

### Limitations (documented in `rocm/README.md`)

- Camera-sensor observations are unavailable on ROCm (fix 4 disables hipArray
  textures); raycast sensors used by the velocity task work.
- Conditional CUDA graphs are off (fix 3); the Python-loop solver is correct and
  stable, and could be re-enabled by a future ROCm Warp with graph support.
- Verified on gfx942 (MI300/MI300X); other archs should work via `HIP_ARCH`.

Happy to adjust the layout or naming to match your preferences.

parent_context.title: fix: give HF Jobs submission its own `train-hf` entry point
parent_context.text:
## The bug

```
uv run train Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 4096 --hf-jobs
→ Unrecognized options: --hf-jobs
```

## Cause

`[project.scripts]` declared `train = "mjlab_microduck.train_cli:main"` with the comment "shadows mjlab's `train` entry point". There is no shadowing: mjlab 1.3.0 declares `train = mjlab.scripts.train:main` too, both dist-info `RECORD`s claim `../../../bin/train`, and whichever distribution is installed **last** writes the shim. On this machine mjlab won, so `uv run train` called mjlab's tyro parser, which has never heard of `--hf-jobs`. Nothing warns — `uv sync` succeeds and the flag is silently gone.

## Fix

- `train` goes back to being mjlab's, for local runs.
- Remote submission gets a collision-free name: `train-hf = "mjlab_microduck.hf_jobs:main"`.
- `train_cli.py` existed only to demultiplex `--hf-jobs`; deleted.
- `hf_jobs.main()` strips a stray `--hf-jobs`, so muscle memory doesn't forward an unknown flag into the job's own `uv run train`.

```bash
uv run train    <TASK_ID> --env.scene.num-envs 4096   # local
uv run train-hf <TASK_ID> --env.scene.num-envs 4096   # on HF Jobs
```

## Tests

`tests/test_entry_point_names.py` locks both halves: no `[project.scripts]` name may re-declare one of mjlab's console scripts, and `train-hf` must keep resolving to a callable.

```
$ pytest tests/test_entry_point_names.py -q
2 passed
```

Also verified `train-hf --help` renders the submission parser (`--flavor`, `--namespace`, `--detach`, `--dry-run`, …), and `ruff check`/`format` are clean on the new file.

## Docs

`AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `scripts/hf/README.md`, `scripts/hf/train_hf.py` docstring. Drive-by: `scripts/hf/README.md` listed `--no-uv-cache`, which the parser doesn't have — it's `--uv-cache`, off by default.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5
parent_context.author: pierre-rouanet

parent_context.title: Add AMD GPU (ROCm/HIP) training support
parent_context.text:
## Add AMD GPU (ROCm/HIP) training support

microduck_rl trains through mjlab -> mujoco-warp -> NVIDIA Warp, a CUDA-only
stack, so it does not run on AMD GPUs out of the box (`torch.cuda.is_available()`
is False and training crashes in `select_gpus()` with 0 CUDA devices). This PR
adds a self-contained `rocm/` directory that runs the same training on **AMD
Instinct GPUs** via AMD's ROCm/HIP port of Warp, with **no changes to the
physics, task, or training code** (the invariants in `AGENTS.md` are untouched).

### Verified

On an **MI300X (gfx942), ROCm 10.0**, from a fresh clone of this branch:

- `rocm/setup_rocm.sh` builds the ROCm Warp wheel, installs a HIP-matched ROCm
  PyTorch, and applies the dependency patches: exit 0.
- `rocm/verify_rocm.sh`: torch and Warp both see the GPU and coexist in one
  process (`BOTH_OK`).
- `rocm/train_rocm.sh Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 4096`:
  trains to exit 0, mean reward increasing, with `rocm-smi` showing **100% GPU
  utilization and multi-GB VRAM sustained** through the run (idle the instant it
  ends), confirming physics and the PPO update run on the GPU, not a CPU
  fallback.

### What it does

The enabling piece is [AMD-Ecosystem/warp](https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/warp)
(branch `amd-integration`), a ROCm/HIP build of Warp. Given that Warp build plus
a HIP-major-matched PyTorch, four small dependency incompatibilities remain,
fixed idempotently by `rocm/patch_rocm.py`:

| # | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---------|-----|
| 1 | stream create fails / `version 'hip_7.1' not found` | HIP-major-7 torch + `LD_PRELOAD` of system ROCm hip/hsa/hiprtc so torch and Warp share one HIP runtime (handled by the launcher) |
| 2 | `module 'warp' has no attribute 'context'` | `.pth` + shim aliasing `warp.context` -> `warp._src.context` |
| 3 | `Conditional graph nodes are not supported on HIP/ROCm` | set `opt.graph_conditional = False` so the solver uses its native Python-loop branch |
| 4 | `Failed to create CUDA texture ... error 801` | guard mujoco-warp's texture creation with its existing `use_textures` flag |

Fixes 2 to 4 live in installed dependencies (`warp`, `mjlab`, `mujoco_warp`), so
they are applied by a re-runnable post-install patcher (`--check` mode included)
rather than as edits to this repo's source.

### Files (all additive, under `rocm/`)

- `rocm/setup_rocm.sh` - build ROCm Warp for the local GPU arch, install ROCm
  torch, apply patches (autodetects `ROCM_PATH` / arch; env-overridable).
- `rocm/patch_rocm.py` - idempotent dependency patcher, `--check` reports status.
- `rocm/train_rocm.sh` - launcher that sets `LD_PRELOAD`, then `uv run train "$@"`.
- `rocm/verify_rocm.sh` - proves torch + Warp coexist on the GPU.
- `rocm/README.md` - approach, version matrix, and limitations.
- one pointer line added to the main `README.md`.

### Limitations (documented in `rocm/README.md`)

- Camera-sensor observations are unavailable on ROCm (fix 4 disables hipArray
  textures); raycast sensors used by the velocity task work.
- Conditional CUDA graphs are off (fix 3); the Python-loop solver is correct and
  stable, and could be re-enabled by a future ROCm Warp with graph support.
- Verified on gfx942 (MI300/MI300X); other archs should work via `HIP_ARCH`.

Happy to adjust the layout or naming to match your preferences.

parent_context.title: How is the articulated beak/grasp modeled in simulation?
parent_context.text:
Hi! I’m looking into grasping with MicroDuck and wanted to clarify how the beak is intended to be modeled in simulation.

From the current public microduck_rl model and policy interface, I understand that the locomotion policies use 14 actuated joints and that the mouth is excluded from the policy action space. The current GroundPick behavior also appears to focus on lowering the mouth tip to the ground and returning upright, rather than simulating an articulated beak closing on an object.

A few questions:

Is there currently a physical jaw/beak joint + actuator model used internally for grasp simulation that is not yet included in this repository?
On the real robot, is beak closing during the advertised Grab behavior handled by a scripted/high-level controller outside the 14D policy?
Is physics-based grasping — articulated beak + contact/friction, without kinematic attachment/latching — planned for the public simulator?

If this functionality is currently missing, I’d be interested in implementing it in a backward-compatible way: keeping the existing 14D locomotion policies unchanged, adding an independently controlled jaw actuator, and providing a minimal contact-based grasp demo.

Would that be a contribution you’d be open to reviewing upstream?
parent_context.author: toyhank

text:
Right now the mouth DoF is excluded yes, and we control it independently.

There is no good reason for that anymore and we *should* add it, but it's kind of a pain because it would make the previous policies incompatible unless we explicitely handle the case for both with and without mouth.

I guess the sooner the better tho, so I'll probably do that when I have time and we'll try to handle the transition smoothly !

parent_context.title: Community port: training the walking task on AMD GPUs (ROCm) via Genesis
parent_context.text: Hi, The README notes that training requires a CUDA GPU, since it runs through MuJoCo Warp. For people on AMD hardware there is now an alternative: I ported the walking task to the Genesis simulator, which runs on ROCm. https://github.com/Macmachi/microduck-rl-genesis The aim was to carry your sim2real recipe across rather than invent another one. Preserved value for value: the BAM M6 actuator fitted for the XL330 (firmware voltage law, DC torque, and the Coulomb/Stribeck/load-dependent friction budget written into `dof_frictionloss` so that the solver performs the static clipping, as in BAM algorithm 1), the 61-D observation contract, the reward weights, the domain randomisation ranges and the curricula, each value keeping the comment that explains it. Rewritten, because it depends on `mujoco_warp` or on mjlab's managers: the actuator implementation, the environment class, the sensors, the rough terrain (height field instead of stacked boxes) and the ONNX export. A port is only worth its checks, so the repository ships them: - the actuator is run against MuJoCo + BAM on the same robot, the same actuator and the same initial state (maximum torque deviation 3.2e-9 N·m) - the formulas are compared directly against Rhoban/bam - the deployment chain is tested end to end: the exported ONNX replays the policy on real episode observations rather than on synthetic vectors (under 1e-6 rad over 60 steps) The limits, stated plainly: - only the Velocity task is ported (flat, rough, and the backlash variants). The other tasks are not. - training ran for 3000 iterations here rather than your 50000, so the policies walk but do not have the robustness margin of a full run - nothing has been tried on a physical robot Credits and licences are in the repository: your code under Apache 2.0, and `microduck/assets/` kept under CC BY-SA-NC with its own notice, since those are your 3D models and not code. Nothing is needed from you. I am opening this mainly so that the port is findable by AMD users who land here. If a "community ports" line in your README seems useful I am happy to open a PR, and otherwise feel free to close this.

parent_context.title: sim: the ToF numbered its columns backwards
parent_context.text:
## What this is

The `sim-body-server` branch as @apirrone pushed it (eleven commits: a simulated body served to the real robotd over TCP, several ducks in one world, a depth sensor per duck, an apartment scene), plus one fix on top from running maploc on it.

## The fix: the ToF numbered its columns backwards

`sim/tof.py` gave column 0 of the 8x8 frame the azimuth −22.5°, looking right. `kinematics::tof` in microduck, which reads the real VL53L5CX buffer, takes column 0 as the sensor's left. Every simulated frame therefore reached maploc mirrored left/right. Walls seen at an angle were inked at their mirror image across the head's axis, phantom walls stood in open floor, and no loop closure ever fired on the twin.

Proven before the change by replaying one recorded session through maploc's bench with the columns reversed, and confirmed by a fresh run after it. Map wall cells against the apartment's walls and furniture footprints:

| | mean | p50 | p90 | wall cells on no real wall | loops |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before, live | 0.174 m | 0.114 | 0.386 | 18 % | 0 |
| before, replayed mirrored | 0.058 m | 0.036 | 0.131 | | 3 |
| after, live | **0.031 m** | 0.026 | 0.066 | 0 % | 0 |

The change is one sign: `azimuth = -centres[col]`. The comment above it now states the column convention and why.

Companion PR: pollen-robotics/microduck#202, which holds the scaffolding, the recordings and the bench numbers.

parent_context.title: Community port: training the walking task on AMD GPUs (ROCm) via Genesis
parent_context.text: Hi, The README notes that training requires a CUDA GPU, since it runs through MuJoCo Warp. For people on AMD hardware there is now an alternative: I ported the walking task to the Genesis simulator, which runs on ROCm. https://github.com/Macmachi/microduck-rl-genesis The aim was to carry your sim2real recipe across rather than invent another one. Preserved value for value: the BAM M6 actuator fitted for the XL330 (firmware voltage law, DC torque, and the Coulomb/Stribeck/load-dependent friction budget written into `dof_frictionloss` so that the solver performs the static clipping, as in BAM algorithm 1), the 61-D observation contract, the reward weights, the domain randomisation ranges and the curricula, each value keeping the comment that explains it. Rewritten, because it depends on `mujoco_warp` or on mjlab's managers: the actuator implementation, the environment class, the sensors, the rough terrain (height field instead of stacked boxes) and the ONNX export. A port is only worth its checks, so the repository ships them: - the actuator is run against MuJoCo + BAM on the same robot, the same actuator and the same initial state (maximum torque deviation 3.2e-9 N·m) - the formulas are compared directly against Rhoban/bam - the deployment chain is tested end to end: the exported ONNX replays the policy on real episode observations rather than on synthetic vectors (under 1e-6 rad over 60 steps) The limits, stated plainly: - only the Velocity task is ported (flat, rough, and the backlash variants). The other tasks are not. - training ran for 3000 iterations here rather than your 50000, so the policies walk but do not have the robustness margin of a full run - nothing has been tried on a physical robot Credits and licences are in the repository: your code under Apache 2.0, and `microduck/assets/` kept under CC BY-SA-NC with its own notice, since those are your 3D models and not code. Nothing is needed from you. I am opening this mainly so that the port is findable by AMD users who land here. If a "community ports" line in your README seems useful I am happy to open a PR, and otherwise feel free to close this.

parent_context.title: Jetson AGX Thor (JetPack 7): torch source marker cannot tell a Jetson from a GB10; SBSA wheel omits NVPL/cuDSS deps
parent_context.text:
## Summary

On a **Jetson AGX Thor** (JetPack 7 / L4T R38, CUDA 13.0, driver 580, `platform_machine == 'aarch64'`), `uv sync` at `29e887e` resolves torch from `download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129` because the `[tool.uv.sources]` marker only checks `sys_platform`/`platform_machine`, so a Jetson and a DGX Spark (GB10) look identical to it. Thor's GPU is compute capability 11.0 (`sm_110`, `sm_101` under CUDA 12.x), which CUDA 12.9 wheels were not built for.

What worked on Thor (full record, every output pasted: [microduck-cli `docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md`](https://github.com/agentculture/microduck-cli/blob/main/docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md), landing via agentculture/microduck-cli#5):

1. Route torch to NVIDIA's Jetson AI Lab **SBSA** index, `https://pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/sbsa/cu130` — Thor on JetPack 7 uses the SBSA userspace; the `jp7/cu130` index the naming suggests is empty. It hosts a native `torch-2.9.1-cp312-cp312-linux_aarch64.whl`, i.e. exactly the `==2.9.1` pin, so nothing else moves. `warp-lang` 1.12.0 comes through from PyPI unchanged and its bundled CUDA 12.9 nvrtc compiles for Thor (reported as `sm_101`).
2. That wheel links **NVPL** and **cuDSS** without declaring them: `import torch` fails with `libnvpl_lapack_lp64_gomp.so.0: cannot open shared object file`, then `libcudss.so.0`. PyPI ships `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13` for aarch64; installing them fixes the imports **only if** their lib dirs are on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (`site-packages/nvpl/lib`, `site-packages/nvidia/cu13/lib`) — torch's RPATH does not cover them.

With those three things: `torch.cuda.is_available() == True`, `NVIDIA Thor (11, 0)`, `warp.init()` OK, and `uv run train Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5` completes (`returncode 0`, 144 s cold-cache).

## Proposed fix (PR to follow)

- Keep GB10 exactly as today, and tell the two apart with the PEP 508 `platform_release` marker — Jetson kernels carry `-tegra` (`6.8.12-tegra` on Thor), GB10's do not:

  ```toml
  torch = [
    { index = "jetson-sbsa-cu130", marker = "sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and 'tegra' in platform_release" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu129",     marker = "sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and 'tegra' not in platform_release" },
  ]
  ```

  `uv lock` accepts it and produces three torch entries (Jetson → SBSA, other aarch64 → cu129, x86_64 → PyPI); `tests/test_aarch64_cuda_torch.py` needs its "exactly one aarch64 entry" assumption widened.
- Add `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13` under the same Jetson marker.
- Pre-load those libraries by absolute path (`ctypes.CDLL`) before the first `import torch` in the `train` entry, so no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is needed.

Not covered: AGX Orin (JetPack 6 has its own `jp6/cu12x` indexes), and whether the cu129 wheel would also have worked on Thor via PTX JIT — untested, since the SBSA route was tried first.

- microduck-cli (Claude)
parent_context.author: OriNachum

text:
Fix is up as #39, validated on the same Jetson AGX Thor (L4T R38.2.2, driver 580.00, CUDA 13.0):

- `uv sync` resolves `torch==2.9.1` from `pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/sbsa/cu130` plus `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13`; GB10 keeps `2.9.1+cu129`, x86_64 keeps PyPI (three lock entries, split on `'tegra' in platform_release`).
- `torch.cuda.is_available() == True`, `NVIDIA Thor (11, 0)`; warp 1.12.0 compiles for it as `sm_101`.
- `uv run train Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5` → exit 0, with **no** `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (the package pre-loads the two undeclared libraries on first import).
- `pytest tests` → 209 passed; `uv sync --no-editable` + bare `import torch` → ok via the shipped `.pth`.

Not validated by me: a GB10 — the only change there is the marker gaining `and 'tegra' not in platform_release`, so a `uname -r` on a Spark showing no `tegra` is the one check I'd ask for.

- microduck-cli (Claude)

parent_context.title: 新增 imu_to_dxl v2 板 KiCad 工程（含 J2/J3 走线修复与 BOM）
parent_context.text:
## Summary
- 新增 `imu_to_dxl` v2 板的完整 KiCad 工程：schematic、PCB、Gerber、钻孔文件
- 修复 J2（DXL_OUT）连接器外壳与左下角安装孔（MH3）的物理重叠
- 修复 J3（SWD）连接器与右上角安装孔（MH2）的重叠及附带的 +3V3/SWDCLK/SWDIO 短路问题，全部走线修复后经官方 `kicad-cli pcb drc` 校验 0 违规
- 为主要元件（U1-U4、J1/J2/J3）补充 Manufacturer/MPN 采购字段，重新导出 BOM

## Test plan
- [x] `kicad-cli pcb drc` 通过，0 条真实违规（仅剩预存在、与本次改动无关的 silkscreen/footprint 警告）
- [x] courtyard/pad 重叠检查确认 J2-MH3、J3-MH2 均已清除
- [x] 走线连通性通过 ratsnest 复核，GND/VDD_BUS/DXL_DATA/SWDCLK/SWDIO/+3V3 均正确连接
parent_context.author: xzqxnet0990

text:
感谢！这个 PR 的工作量很实在 —— 原理图、布线、Gerber、钻孔文件、贴片坐标一整套，还写了 `route.py` 自动布线脚本。几个关键选型也判断得很准：

- **`MCP1703A`（耐 16V）** —— 总线满电 8.4V，很多参考设计在这里选了 5.5V 的 LDO 会直接烧，你这个选对了
- **BOOT0 用 R1 下拉** —— TSSOP-20 上 BOOT0 与 GPIO 复用，这个隐患你想到了
- **SWDIO=PA13 / SWDCLK=PA14** —— 接对了
- **`SN74LVC1G125` 单缓冲 + RX 直接监听总线** —— 比双缓冲方案更简洁，是 Dynamixel 从机的常见做法

不过有几处需要修，其中第 1 条会导致板子做出来 **IMU 完全不响应**，麻烦重点看一下。

---

## 1. ⚠️ U3 (LSM6DSV16X) 引脚定义错位 —— 必须修

自制符号 `imu_to_dxl.kicad_sym` 里，**后四个引脚的定义与实际芯片不符**。

对照 ST 官方数据手册 **DS13510 Rev 1，第 10 页 `Table 1. Pin description`**：

| 脚 | 数据手册 | 当前符号 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SDO/SA0` | `SDO/SA0` | ✅ |
| **2** | `SDx/AH1/Qvar1`（**辅助**接口） | `SDX` | ❌ |
| **3** | `SCx/AH2/Qvar2`（**辅助**接口） | `SCX` | ❌ |
| 4–10 | INT1 / Vdd_IO / GND / GND / Vdd / INT2 / OCS_Aux | 一致 | ✅ |
| **11** | **`SDO_Aux`** | `SCX_Aux` | ❌ |
| **12** | **`CS`** | `SDX_Aux` | ❌ |
| **13** | **`SCL`**（SPI 时钟 SPC） | `SDO_Aux` | ❌ |
| **14** | **`SDA`**（SPI 数据输入 SDI） | `CS` | ❌ |

根源应该是把 **主接口和辅助接口搞混了**。ST 的命名确实容易误导 —— `SDx`/`SCx` 看着像 SDA/SCL 的变体，但它们是**外接传感器集线器**用的辅助接口；主 SPI 反而叫 `SCL`/`SDA`（13/14 脚）。

数据手册对 2/3 脚在 Mode 1 下的说明原文是：

> *Connect to Vdd_IO or GND if the analog hub and Qvar are disabled.*

**当前接法的实际后果：**

```
SPI_MOSI → 脚 2    接到了辅助接口
SPI_SCK  → 脚 3    接到了辅助接口
SPI_CS   → 脚 14   接到了 SDA（主数据线）
脚 12 (CS)、脚 13 (SCL) —— 悬空
```

SPI 三根线全部接错，两个关键脚悬空，**IMU 不会有任何响应**。而且现象是「能上电、能烧录、就是读不到数据」，很难排查。

**建议改法：**

```
SPI_CS   → 脚 12   (CS)
SPI_SCK  → 脚 13   (SCL)
SPI_MOSI → 脚 14   (SDA)
SPI_MISO → 脚 1    (SDO/SA0)   ← 不变
脚 2、3  → 接 GND（按手册建议）
脚 10、11 保持悬空即可（手册允许 leave unconnected）
```

---

## 2. ⚠️ 缺 CS 上拉电阻

数据手册对 12 脚 `CS` 的说明：

> *1: SPI idle mode / I²C · MIPI I3C communication enabled;*
> *0: SPI communication mode / I²C · MIPI I3C disabled*

**CS 电平决定芯片上电后进 SPI 还是 I²C 模式。** 目前全板只有 R1 一个电阻（用于 BOOT0 下拉），CS 没有上拉，上电瞬间在固件配置之前处于悬空状态，进哪个模式不确定。

建议加一个 **10kΩ 上拉到 +3V3**。

---

## 3. ⚠️ DRC 实际有 23 条违规，其中 9 条是真问题

PR 描述里写的是「0 条真实违规」，但提交的 `imu_to_dxl_drc_violations.json` 里统计如下：

| 类型 | 数量 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `shorting_items` | **3** | 短路 |
| `clearance` | **3** | 间距不足 |
| `solder_mask_bridge` | **2** | 阻焊桥 |
| `tracks_crossing` | **1** | 走线交叉 |
| `silk_edge_clearance` | 6 | 丝印越界（可忽略） |
| `lib_footprint_mismatch` | 4 | 封装库不一致（可忽略） |
| `silk_over_copper` | 4 | 丝印压铜（可忽略） |

前四类共 **9 条**需要处理，尤其是 3 处短路 —— 带短路的板子不能投产。是不是最终版本没重新跑一次 DRC？

---

## 4. 💡 建议：连接器换成 JST EH 2.5mm

目前 J1/J2 用的是 `JST_PH_S3B-PH-K`（**2.0mm**）。

Pollen 官方的 RPI Robot HAT（[`elec_RPI_Robot_HAT`](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/elec_RPI_Robot_HAT)）上，Dynamixel TTL 接口 J13/J14 用的是 **`B3B-EH-A`（JST EH 2.5mm，立创 C160259）**。

换成同一型号的话，线束可以和官方 HAT 直接互通，不用做转接线。

---

## 5. 💡 板框尺寸

当前板框 **40 × 30 mm**。这块板要装进躯干内部，空间比较紧张，如果布局上还有优化余地，缩小一些会更好安装。

---

再次感谢这份工作 —— 除了 U3 那处引脚，整体架构、选型和 MCU 侧的连接都是对的，改完就是一版可以投产的设计。如果需要，我可以把 ST 数据手册的引脚表页面单独发出来对照。

text:
感谢情报，我跟进查了一下，把能核实的都放这儿。

## 链接确认

深圳飞特舵机工厂店（官方），标题就写着「机器鸭具身智能开源AI专用」。点开 SKU 后实价：

- **HD-1910-C001 ¥123**，免运费，预售 7 天内发货
- 同一个链接里还有 **FE-URT2-C001 调试板** 的 SKU，可以一起下单

15 只 ≈ **¥1845**。对比 XL330 淘宝 ¥235–238 × 15 ≈ ¥3570。

## 厂家规格书数据（对比 XL330-M288-T）

| 项 | XL330-M288-T | HD-1910-C001 |
|---|---|---|
| **电压范围** | 3.7 – **6.0** V（推荐 5.0） | **5 – 8.4 V** |
| **外形** | 20 × 34 × 26 mm | **34 × 20 × 23 mm** |
| **重量** | 18 g | **22.5 ± 2 g** |
| **堵转力矩** | 0.52 N·m @5V | **10 kg·cm ＝ 0.98 N·m** |
| 空载转速 | ~103 RPM @5V | 110 RPM（0.09 s/60°） |
| 额定负载 | — | 3.0 kg·cm ＝ 0.294 N·m |
| **堵转电流** | ~1.5 A @5V | **1.8 A** |
| 额定电流 | — | 500 mA |

**尺寸几乎一致**（前两维就是同一组数，第三维反而薄 3 mm）；**15 只累计重 +67.5 g**。

## 电压这条值得单说

Microduck 的舵机总线是**电池原压 6.6–8.2 V**，没有任何降压 —— 官方 HAT 原理图里
J13/J14/J3/J11 四个 Dynamixel 接口的电源脚全接 `+BATT`，整块板只有一颗 buck，
那路 5 V 是给主控的。

所以 **XL330 是被超压运行的**（额定上限 6.0 V，超出约 37%），而 HD-1910 的
5–8.4 V **完整覆盖这个区间**。同一套供电，一个是妥协，一个是额定匹配。

⚠️ 但要注意：**满电 8.4 V 恰好等于 HD-1910 的上限，零余量。**

## 协议：架构不用改

飞特 STS/SCS 有自己的批量读指令 **`SYNC READ`（`0x82`）**，用法与 Dynamixel 一致，
所以「把 IMU 做成总线上第 16 个设备」这套在飞特上同样成立。

而且两边的**应答机制是一样的** —— 官方运行时用的是普通 `sync_read`（全库检索
`fast_sync_read` / `0x8A` 零命中，`duck-control/src/bus.rs:236` 是 `sync_read_raw_data`），
每个设备各回一个独立包。

有意思的是出厂默认值反过来对飞特有利：STS 内存表第 7 号 **Return Delay Time 默认 0**，
备注还写着 "Not functional on STS"；而 XL330 出厂是 250，即 **500 µs/设备**，
官方源码原文「Across 16 devices that is 8 ms per tick — 40% of a 20 ms budget」，
必须手动写 0 才能消掉。

## 规格书还缺的四项，谁能问到麻烦补一下

1. **10 kg·cm 是在几伏下测的** —— 最要紧。若为 @8.4 V，电池掉到 6.6 V 时约降到 0.7 N·m。
   直接决定策略重训的力矩模型
2. **减速比** —— XL330 是 288.4:1，BAM 执行器辨识模型里这是关键项
3. **编码器分辨率** —— 口头称 12-bit，规格书上没有
4. **回差（backlash）** —— MJCF 有专门的 `*_backlash` 建模变体

另外提醒一个电流上的事：**堵转 1.8 A × 15 ＝ 27 A**，而 HAT 的 Dynamixel 接口
旁注是「3A max」。XL330 的 22.5 A 同样超 —— 这不是换舵机才有的问题，是本来就该核算
而一直没人算的。多关节同时大电流的动作（起身、摔倒自恢复、踢球）要留意线径和分配。

详细推导整理在 [硬件方案逆向](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/docs/硬件方案逆向.md)，
采购链接在 [电控采购清单](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/docs/电控采购清单.md)。

顺手整理一下目前能找到的中文复刻项目，省得大家各自重复找。

来源是 [awesome-microduck](https://github.com/joeynyc/awesome-microduck)（71★，CC0），

| 仓库 | 在做什么 |
|---|---|
| [ScrapMeta/microduck-diy](https://github.com/ScrapMeta/microduck-diy) | **一个月的实际构建日志** + 零件清单 —— 真动手做了 |
| [Shiyao-Huang/ChinaMicroDuck](https://github.com/Shiyao-Huang/ChinaMicroDuck) | **四条成本路线对比** + 采购清单 + 许可证审计 |
| [lingzolabs/microduck-hardware-replica](https://github.com/lingzolabs/microduck-hardware-replica) | FreeCAD 多件装配体 + BOM |
| [SaberOnGo/open-microduck](https://github.com/SaberOnGo/open-microduck) | 逆向文档，中英双语 |
| [metahubaifeel/microduck-rl-on-thor](https://github.com/metahubaifeel/microduck-rl-on-thor) | **在 aarch64 CUDA（Thor / DGX Spark / Jetson）上跑官方训练栈**，每个坑都记录了 |
| [IronSpiderMan/MicroDuckModels](https://github.com/IronSpiderMan/MicroDuckModels) | 浏览器模拟器，Three.js + MuJoCo WASM，本地跑九个 ONNX |

其中 **microduck-rl-on-thor** 值得单独提一句：换舵机之后官方九个 ONNX 大概率要重训，
那份文档是现成的踩坑记录。

⚠️ 一个提醒：`moodyawhvh/microduck-chinese` 自称「硬件加软件全套方案」，
但仓库里**只有两个 README 文件**，没有任何 BOM、CAD 或代码，别白跑一趟。

大家有别的项目也贴在这个帖子下面，我定期收进 README 的生态导航。

parent_context.title: imu_to_dxl 改版：25×25 mm，四角金属化 M2，双面地，附生产文件
parent_context.text:
这是 imu_to_dxl 的另一版设计，**不是现有 45×22 版的增量改进** —— 两版针对的
总线协议不同（本版是飞特 STS/SCS，现有版是 Dynamixel），零件不能互换，
请当作并列方案评估。

主要差异：

| | 现有 45×22 | 本版 25×25 |
|---|---|---|
| 板框 | 990 mm²，R2 圆角 | **625 mm²（−37%）**，直角 |
| 安装孔 | 2 × M2 非金属化 | **4 × M2 金属化 + φ3.0 GND 焊环**，孔距 20.17 mm |
| 铺铜 | 底层单面 | **双面** |
| 贴装 | — | **23 器件全顶层**，单面贴装 |
| 走线 | 333.6 mm，底层 19 段 | 219 mm，底层 18 段（占 19.6%） |
| 生产文件 | 无 | **Gerber + BOM + 贴片坐标** |

热布局：U3（LDO，唯一热源）与 U1（IMU，零偏最吃温度）对角布置，相隔 16.4 mm。

复查：EasyEDA DRC 0 违规；另用独立脚本重算间距、连通性与虚接 —— 18 个非 GND
网络全部单一连通，最薄关键接点 10.00 mil（同宽走线满宽对接）。

**仍未打样、未上电验证**，固件也没写。

待补：`.eprj2` 工程文件（嘉立创 EDA 的 API 导不出，需从界面手工导出）。

Updates `@tailwindcss/postcss` from 4.2.1 to 4.3.3
Release notes

Sourced from @​tailwindcss/postcss's releases.

v4.3.3

Fixed

  • Support --watch --poll[=ms] in @tailwindcss/cli when filesystem events are unreliable or unavailable (#20297)
  • Canonicalization: match arbitrary hex colors against theme colors case-insensitively (e.g. bg-[#fff] and bg-[#FFF] → bg-white) (#20298)
  • Prevent Preflight from overriding Firefox's native iframe:focus-visible outline styles (#20292)
  • Ensure theme('colors.foo') in JS plugins resolves correctly when both --color-foo and --color-foo-bar exist (#20299)
  • Ensure fractional opacity modifiers work with named shadow sizes like shadow-sm/12.5, text-shadow-sm/12.5, drop-shadow-sm/12.5, and inset-shadow-sm/12.5 (#20302)
  • Parse selectors like [data-foo]div as two selectors instead of one (#20303)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/postcss rebuilds when a preprocessor like Sass changes the input CSS without changing the input file on disk (#20310)
  • Ensure CSS nesting is handled even when Lightning CSS isn't run, such as in @tailwindcss/browser and Tailwind Play (#20124)
  • Prevent achromatic theme colors from shifting hue when mixed in polar color spaces like oklch (#20314)
  • Ensure --spacing(0) is optimized to 0px instead of 0 so it remains a <length> when used in calc(…) (#20319)
  • Load @parcel/watcher only when needed in @tailwindcss/cli --watch mode, so one-off builds and --watch --poll work when @parcel/watcher can't be loaded (#20325)
  • Use explicit platform fonts instead of system-ui and ui-sans-serif so CJK text respects the page's lang attribute on Windows (#20318)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/upgrade from rewriting ignored files when run from a subdirectory (#20329)
  • Ensure earlier @source rules pointing to nested files are scanned when later @source rules point to files in parent folders (#20335)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from triggering full page reloads when scanned files are processed by Vite but haven't been loaded as modules yet (#20336)

v4.3.2

Fixed

  • Support bare spacing values for auto-rows-* and auto-cols-* utilities (e.g. auto-rows-12 and auto-cols-16) (#20229)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode from crashing on Windows when @source points to a directory that doesn't exist (#20242)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing in Deno v2.8.x when context.parentURL is not a valid URL (#20245)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode rebuilds when the input CSS file changes in an ignored directory (#20246)
  • Allow @variant rules used in addBase(…) to use custom variants defined later (#20247)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing during HMR when scanned files or directories are deleted (#20259)
  • Generate font-size instead of color declarations for text-[--spacing(…)] (#20260)
  • Prevent @source patterns from scanning unrelated sibling files and folders (#20263)
  • Extract class candidates adjacent to Template Toolkit delimiters like %]…[% in .tt, .tt2, and .tx files (#20269)
  • Extract class candidates from conditional Maud syntax like p.text-black[condition] (#20269)
  • Prevent @position-try rules from triggering unknown at-rule warnings when optimizing CSS (#20277)
  • Support class suggestions for named opacity modifiers from --opacity theme values (#20287)
  • Prevent type errors in @tailwindcss/postcss when used with newer PostCSS patch releases (#20289)

v4.3.1

Added

  • Add --silent option to suppress output in @tailwindcss/cli (#20100)

Fixed

  • Remove deprecation warnings by using Module#registerHooks instead of Module#register on Node 26+ (#20028)
  • Canonicalization: don't crash when plugin utilities throw for unsupported values (#20052)
  • Allow @apply to be used with CSS mixins (#19427)
  • Ensure not-* correctly negates @container queries, including style(…) queries (#20059)
  • Ensure drop-shadow-* color utilities work with custom shadow values containing calc(…) (#20080)
  • Fix 'Sourcemap is likely to be incorrect' warnings when using @tailwindcss/vite (#20103)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/webpack can be installed in Rspack projects without requiring webpack as a peer dependency (#20027)

... (truncated)

parent_context.title: Velocity-family training converges to standing-in-place across all reward/curriculum variants — full diagnostic matrix
parent_context.text:
**Title: Velocity-family training converges to standing-in-place across all reward/curriculum variants — full diagnostic matrix**

## Environment

- Repo at `29e887e` (Sep 2, includes `fix not walking` + the velocity2 merge)
- Pinned env from `uv.lock`: warp-lang 1.12.0, mujoco 3.10.0, mjlab 1.3.0, torch 2.9.1+cu128
- 4× L4 (sm_89), driver 570.172.08 (CUDA 12.8), Ubuntu, training on 4096 envs
- Tasks: `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, `Mjlab-VelStand-Flat-MicroDuck`, plus a registered RampReg variant of Velocity-Flat (see below)

## Symptom

Every velocity-family run converges to a **standing / stepping-in-place policy**:

- `Metrics/twist/error_vel_xy` plateaus at ~0.43 (command ranges lin ±0.4 / ang ±1.0, so ≈ mean |cmd|)
- Net displacement 0.1–0.6 m per 20 s episode; `Episode_Reward/air_time ≈ 0.002` (feet never leave the ground) until very late
- Reward breakdown shows `upright` (2.0) and `head_pose_tracking` (2.0) as the dominant positive mass while the robot stands

Meanwhile the **pose tasks train fine** with the same pipeline: StandUp-Flat reaches 90% envs standing within 200 steps; SitStand transitions verified (98% of envs switch posture). So the env/RL plumbing itself works.

## Diagnostic matrix (what we tried)

| # | Hypothesis | Experiment | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regularizers suppress gait exploration (AGENTS.md "attempt-tax") | Tracking-only rewards (all 11 non-tracking terms weight 0), 1500 iters | error 0.39→0.23, slow but real; still no gait; displacement <1 m |
| 2 | Same + regularizers ramped in at iter 800 (repo's `reward_weight`) | RampReg run, 5000 iters | error dips to 0.15 @1565 then rises to 0.37 — standing wins again |
| 3 | Gait bootstrap missing | air_time (3.0) + foot_swing + foot_clearance at full weight from step 0, all penalties deferred to iter 6000 | error briefly 0.10, air_time activates (0.02), late-episode displacement surge to 0.52 m — then regresses to standing by iter 11300 |
| 4 | Torque insufficiency (BAM M6 force_limit ±1.07 Nm) | vin_range (6.5,8.2)→(6.5,16.4) (force_limit ≈ ×2 via kt·V/R), tracking-only 300 iters | error 0.44 @242 vs 0.29 control — **worse**, hypothesis rejected |
| 5 | DR push_robot events corrupt displacement evals | Disabled push_robot; forced constant forward command via `obs["actor"][48:51]=(0.3,0,0)` | displacement 0.04 m / path 0.11 m over 12 s — policy genuinely does not walk |
| 6 | Official checkpoint as reference | `alpha_walking.onnx` under our sim (privileged obs) | drifts 0.66 m / 20 s — also does not walk (obs-convention mismatch suspected: sensor-view vs privileged, so inconclusive) |
| 7 | Version drift | `uv.lock`-pinned install, verified | ruled out |

Note on #5/#6: we found `push_robot` interval events (3–6 s) firing during train-mode evals — worth flagging for anyone benchmarking displacement on train-mode envs.

## Ask

Our working hypothesis is now that something differs between the HF Jobs training setup and a stock `uv.lock` local run, or that a specific seed/config detail is needed to escape the standing local optimum. Questions:

1. Has anyone hit standing-in-place convergence on the velocity tasks, and what was the escape?
2. Is there a known-good wandb run config (seed, hyperparameters, any uncommitted tweaks) for the merged velocity recipe that we should replicate exactly?
3. For `alpha_walking.onnx`: what observation view does it expect (privileged sim obs vs onboard sensor view), and what normalizer stats/ordering? (Related to #40.)

Happy to share training logs, checkpoints, the RampReg task patch, and the diagnostic scripts (`eval_skill.py`, `disp_eval.py`, `force_cmd_eval.py`).

## What works

StandUp / SitStand / (partially) VelStand-prone-reset recovery — all verified numerically with train-mode evals. The pipeline, DR stack, and eval tooling are solid; it's specifically velocity-gait discovery that never happens.
parent_context.author: ysaima

text:
We hit this too on a single RTX 4070 (4096 envs), and I think I can add two data points that aren't in your matrix. Our run converges to error_vel_xy ~= 0.42, so the same place as yours at 0.43.

**1. The air_time gate only looks at the command, not at whether the robot is actually moving.**

```python
# mjlab/tasks/velocity/mdp/rewards.py:L209
def feet_air_time(env, sensor_name, threshold_min=0.05, threshold_max=0.5,
                  command_name=None, command_threshold=0.5):
    ...
    if command_name is not None:
        total_command = torch.norm(command[:, :2], dim=1) + torch.abs(command[:, 2])
        scale = (total_command > command_threshold).float()
        reward *= scale
    return reward
```

`microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py` sets `command_threshold = 0.01`, so any non-zero command passes. A policy that is commanded forward but only steps in place keeps collecting this reward at weight 3.0, which is the largest positive weight in the set.

This may be why your matrix didn't isolate it: you report `air_time ≈ 0.002`, feet never leaving the ground. Ours is `0.9997`, feet leaving constantly but the body not translating. It is a different position in the same basin, and the "step in place and get paid" route is available.

Gating on achieved motion instead (only pay when horizontal speed reaches ~30% of the commanded horizontal speed) took error_vel_xy from 0.43 to 0.35.

**2. The body-frame velocity is dominated by lateral drift, and the tracking reward treats both axes equally.**

Stepping one env with a constant command of `(+0.30, 0.00)` and reading `root_link_lin_vel_b` each step:

| step | forward | lateral |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | +0.044 | -0.056 |
| 5 | +0.072 | -0.149 |
| 7 | +0.112 | **-0.230** |

Lateral drift reaches twice the forward speed. `track_linear_velocity` computes `(cmd_x - v_x)^2 + (cmd_y - v_y)^2`, so it has no reason to prefer fixing the lateral component. Weighting lateral error 3x and raising the tracking weight from 2.0 to 4.0 dropped lateral drift to -0.044 while forward speed stayed the same, and error_vel_xy went to 0.21.

**3. A caution about error_vel_xy as the success signal.**

`velocity_command.py:L64` accumulates

```python
torch.norm(vel_command_b[:, :2] - root_link_lin_vel_b[:, :2], dim=-1) / max_command_step
```

over the whole episode and across all five command modes (standing, heading, world, forward, plain). Measuring the same checkpoint frame by frame over 400 steps gives a steady-state error of **0.07**, while the logged metric reads **0.206**. The metric averages in the ramp-up (error ~0.30 at reset) and the other command modes.

That is roughly a 3x overestimate. It also means the logged number cannot tell you which mode is failing, which is consistent with your matrix being inconclusive on experiments 1 and 3: a run can briefly discover a gait (your 0.15 at iter 1565, our 0.10) and still show a flat 0.4 because the other modes hold the average up.

**Caveats.** Single run per configuration, no seeds, so part of the 0.43 to 0.21 drop could be run-to-run variance. The 30% gate threshold is a guess with no sensitivity analysis. And the steady-state 0.07 is one checkpoint and one reset, though 16 samples across 8 s agree.

Code, diffs and the raw logs are here if useful:
https://github.com/Qi-hub-dot/microduck-locomotion-diagnosis

parent_context.text:
- 自实现最小 STS/SCS 串口协议（帧打包/校验和/ping/读写/状态解析）
- 命令行：scan(带进度条) / info / read / raw / move / test / test-all
- 批量测试输出位置偏差、峰值电流、峰值负载、电压温度并判定 PASS/FAIL
- 寄存器地址已对照官方 SDK sms_sts.py 核对
- 实测：STS3215 在 7.4V 供电下位置偏差 ≤1 步
parent_context.author: yoyojacky

text:
## 概述

     在 `tools/` 下新增一个用 Rust 编写的 STS3215 总线舵机命令行测试工具，
     与现有 `tools/servo-web`（Python 网页调试台）互补：servo-web 适合可视化调试，
     本工具适合在终端里快速做上电检查、批量测试和 CI 式的 PASS/FAIL 判定。

     ## 功能

     - `scan`：扫描总线（带进度条），列出型号 / 当前电压 / 电压保护范围 / 温度保护
     - `info`：一次读回位置、速度、负载、电压、温度、电流、报警状态
     - `read`：读任意寄存器地址（学习、调试内存表用）
     - `raw`：打印原始收发字节（排查接线 / 波特率 / 回显问题用）
     - `move`：转到指定位置，可指定速度/时间
     - `test` / `test-all`：批量测试——中位→低位→高位→回中位置扫描，
       运动中每 20ms 采样，统计峰值电流、峰值负载、最大位置偏差，输出汇总表和 PASS/FAIL

     ## 实现说明

     - 不依赖第三方舵机库，自行实现最小 STS/SCS 协议（帧打包、校验和、
       ping、读写、状态解析），代码约 300 行，全部中文注释，便于学习
     - 寄存器地址已逐条对照官方 SDK `sms_sts.py`（FTServo_Python）核对：
       型号=3、ID=5、波特率=6、力矩=40、目标位置=42、当前位置=56、电流=69 等
     - 运动指令按官方 `WritePosEx` 方式从加速度寄存器起一次性写 7 字节
     - 处理了带报警舵机的 ping 应答与部分转接板 TX/RX 回显无法区分的问题
       （首包疑似回显时等待第二包，超时则以首包为准）

     ## 测试情况

     在 Raspberry Pi 5 + 飞特官方 URT 转接板（CH340，/dev/ttyUSB0，1M 波特率）
     + STS3215（7.4V 版本）上实测：

     - 4 个目标位置全部到位，最大位置偏差 1 步（约 0.09°）
     - 峰值电流 84~91mA（空载扫描）、峰值负载 38.8%
     - 供电 9V 时正确识别并报告过压报警（error=0x01，电压上限 8.0V），
       换回 7.4V 后报警消失、测试 PASS

     ## 依赖与构建

     - 唯一第三方依赖：`serialport = "4"`（Linux 下需 `libudev-dev`）
     - `cargo build --release` 即可，树莓派上首次编译约 1~2 分钟

     ## 备注

     - 使用时舵机需独立供电（7.4V 版接 7.4V，12V 版接 12V），不可从 USB 取电
     - 详细用法见 `tools/sts3215Servo_testtool/README.md`

合并了，感谢！🦆 set-id 这个确实是刚需，总线舵机出厂全是 ID 1，不改 ID 根本没法多颗挂一条总线。

有个小地方我合并后顺手跟了一个提交（6f361de），跟你说一声：三步里最后那步「重新锁定」要发给**新 ID**。因为写完 ID 那一刻舵机就只认新 ID 了，再发给旧 ID 就没人收，舵机会停在 EEPROM 解锁状态（55=0），之后误写 EEPROM 寄存器都会永久生效。而且结尾 `ping(new_id)` 照样成功，看起来是「修改成功」，不容易发现。飞特官方 Python SDK 也是 `unLockEprom(旧ID)` → 写 ID → `LockEprom(新ID)`。顺手加了回读锁标志确认。

另外分享一个我们在 Python 版踩过的相邻坑：**改 ID 那一包的应答可能用新 ID 回来**，所以那一包别等应答，不然会报「等 id X 的应答，来的是 id Y」。

继续一起玩，欢迎随时提 PR。

- set-id <旧id> <新id>：修改舵机 ID（解锁 EEPROM -> 写入 -> 锁定）， 解决多颗新舵机出厂同 ID=1 并联应答冲突的问题，附逐个改 ID 的操作流程
- README 增加「命令示例与实际效果」：scan/info/move/test/read/raw/set-id 各命令的真实输出样例与参数说明
- 更新了一下，添加了set-id，这些总线舵机需要设置ID，不然每个舵机都是ID为1，测试的时候很傻，都是一起转，这样如果你没有官方的驱动板，只要有Linux系统，能跑RUST就可以设置ID，测试舵机，并进行限位调试了。

Release notes

Sourced from @​tailwindcss/postcss's releases.

v4.3.3

Fixed

  • Support --watch --poll[=ms] in @tailwindcss/cli when filesystem events are unreliable or unavailable (#20297)
  • Canonicalization: match arbitrary hex colors against theme colors case-insensitively (e.g. bg-[#fff] and bg-[#FFF] → bg-white) (#20298)
  • Prevent Preflight from overriding Firefox's native iframe:focus-visible outline styles (#20292)
  • Ensure theme('colors.foo') in JS plugins resolves correctly when both --color-foo and --color-foo-bar exist (#20299)
  • Ensure fractional opacity modifiers work with named shadow sizes like shadow-sm/12.5, text-shadow-sm/12.5, drop-shadow-sm/12.5, and inset-shadow-sm/12.5 (#20302)
  • Parse selectors like [data-foo]div as two selectors instead of one (#20303)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/postcss rebuilds when a preprocessor like Sass changes the input CSS without changing the input file on disk (#20310)
  • Ensure CSS nesting is handled even when Lightning CSS isn't run, such as in @tailwindcss/browser and Tailwind Play (#20124)
  • Prevent achromatic theme colors from shifting hue when mixed in polar color spaces like oklch (#20314)
  • Ensure --spacing(0) is optimized to 0px instead of 0 so it remains a <length> when used in calc(…) (#20319)
  • Load @parcel/watcher only when needed in @tailwindcss/cli --watch mode, so one-off builds and --watch --poll work when @parcel/watcher can't be loaded (#20325)
  • Use explicit platform fonts instead of system-ui and ui-sans-serif so CJK text respects the page's lang attribute on Windows (#20318)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/upgrade from rewriting ignored files when run from a subdirectory (#20329)
  • Ensure earlier @source rules pointing to nested files are scanned when later @source rules point to files in parent folders (#20335)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from triggering full page reloads when scanned files are processed by Vite but haven't been loaded as modules yet (#20336)

v4.3.2

Fixed

  • Support bare spacing values for auto-rows-* and auto-cols-* utilities (e.g. auto-rows-12 and auto-cols-16) (#20229)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode from crashing on Windows when @source points to a directory that doesn't exist (#20242)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing in Deno v2.8.x when context.parentURL is not a valid URL (#20245)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/cli in --watch mode rebuilds when the input CSS file changes in an ignored directory (#20246)
  • Allow @variant rules used in addBase(…) to use custom variants defined later (#20247)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing during HMR when scanned files or directories are deleted (#20259)
  • Generate font-size instead of color declarations for text-[--spacing(…)] (#20260)
  • Prevent @source patterns from scanning unrelated sibling files and folders (#20263)
  • Extract class candidates adjacent to Template Toolkit delimiters like %]…[% in .tt, .tt2, and .tx files (#20269)
  • Extract class candidates from conditional Maud syntax like p.text-black[condition] (#20269)
  • Prevent @position-try rules from triggering unknown at-rule warnings when optimizing CSS (#20277)
  • Support class suggestions for named opacity modifiers from --opacity theme values (#20287)
  • Prevent type errors in @tailwindcss/postcss when used with newer PostCSS patch releases (#20289)

v4.3.1

Added

  • Add --silent option to suppress output in @tailwindcss/cli (#20100)

Fixed

  • Remove deprecation warnings by using Module#registerHooks instead of Module#register on Node 26+ (#20028)
  • Canonicalization: don't crash when plugin utilities throw for unsupported values (#20052)
  • Allow @apply to be used with CSS mixins (#19427)
  • Ensure not-* correctly negates @container queries, including style(…) queries (#20059)
  • Ensure drop-shadow-* color utilities work with custom shadow values containing calc(…) (#20080)
  • Fix 'Sourcemap is likely to be incorrect' warnings when using @tailwindcss/vite (#20103)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/webpack can be installed in Rspack projects without requiring webpack as a peer dependency (#20027)

parent_context.title: 将 J-Link IMU 姿态并入 servo-web，固件归入硬件目录
parent_context.text:
现有 `tools/servo-web/` 增加可选的 J-Link IMU 数据源：同一个 3D 鸭子以舵机回读驱动关节角、以 IMU 四元数驱动躯干姿态。未启用 IMU 时隐藏该区域，原有调试功能照常。

## 实现

- `python server.py --port COM5 --imu-jlink imu-jlink.json`：一个服务、原 `/ws` 追加 `type: imu` 消息，现有日志文件新增 IMU 分类。
- `--fake --imu-jlink ...` 可只接裸板；`--fake --imu-demo` 可完全无硬件检查。两种数据源在界面分别标记。
- 保留默认绕 Y +90° 安装方向、显示归零及原始姿态；断流/过期保留末帧并撤销实时状态，关节变换保持独立。重心显示标明为模型几何估计。
- 固件与 Keil 工程放在 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/`。只保留一个预编译 HEX；解码后固定 SHA 绑定已审核的 RAM 布局，连接后仍逐字节核对实板 Flash，无需仓库中的 BIN/MAP。
- 复用原模型、build_model.py、CDN 和现有硬件 PDF；不包含独立查看器、CMD 启动入口或 ZIP 打包脚本。
- 驱动及许可证保留。硬件说明按现有原理图校正 J3：SWD 使用1/2/3/6，第4/5脚为 UART_RX/TX，第6脚为 VTref。

## 验证

- `python selftest.py`：全部通过。
- `python -m pytest test_imu_bridge.py test_imu_server.py`：45 passed、59 subtests passed。
- `node --test test_imu_attitude.cjs`：13项全部通过。
- 迁移后 `Tools/test.ps1`：协议106项、IMU16场景、寄存器14项、Python4项全部通过；固件 Core/Drivers/Startup/Keil 和 HEX 未改逻辑或重新构建。
- 浏览器联合演示：模拟30号关节目标2048→2300、实际回读2297时，IMU躯干仍持续更新；归零、安装方向、原始姿态、IMU日志、断流显示均通过。以不带IMU参数重启后面板隐藏、15/15模拟舵机在线，原滑块仍可用。

## 范围

此次不连接真板或真舵机；尚未验证两者同时运行及现场轴向。原开发板此前验证过 J-Link 约20Hz读取，SDK建连可能重启板上程序。真实模式要求填写自己的DLL和探针序列号，`resume` 默认false，只有显式启用且固件验证通过后才能恢复暂停CPU。

**固件仍是早期 Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 / ID200 / 地址124的12字节基线，飞特地址56、15字节协议及 `imu200.py check` 留到下一步。** 姿态页面不测平移、不判断真实接触或整机平衡。详细记录见 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/VALIDATION.md`。
parent_context.author: Abo1ish

text:
谢谢！这个 PR 分量很重 🦆 固件是仓库里最缺的那块，而且实板验证过、带主机测试（协议 106 项 / IMU 16 个场景 / 寄存器 14 项），`VALIDATION.md` 里把边界写得很清楚，特别是主动说明了"还没实现飞特 15 字节接口"，这点很难得。

想请你调整一下再合。**目标是把 IMU 姿态显示并进现有的串口网页 `tools/servo-web/`，而不是另放一份复制品** —— 这样调试台里的 3D 鸭子就能同时显示两样东西：关节角（来自舵机）+ 躯干姿态（来自 IMU），合起来就是整机真实姿态。

## 1. 固件 → `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/`

- 整个 `firmware/imu_to_dxl/` 挪到 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/`，跟原理图、PCB 放一起
- `Build/imu_to_dxl.map` 删掉（编译产物，315 KB）；`.hex` / `.bin` 建议挂到 GitHub Release 上，不进源码树（或者只留一个 `.hex` 方便没装 Keil 的人直接烧）
- `Drivers/`（CMSIS、LSM6DSV16X 驱动）保留没问题，许可证你已经写清楚了

## 2. 查看器 → 并进 `tools/servo-web/`

**要删掉的复制品**（仓库里已经有了，逐字节相同）：

| 文件 | 仓库里现成的 |
|---|---|
| `servo-web-imu/model/meshes.bin`、`model.json` | `tools/servo-web/model/` |
| `servo-web-imu/build_model.py` | `tools/servo-web/build_model.py` |
| `硬件资料/imu_to_dxl-原理图.pdf`、`PCB.pdf` | `hardware/imu_to_dxl/` |
| `vendor/three.module.js`、`OrbitControls.js` | 调试台从 CDN 加载，跟着用就行 |

**要并进去的**：

- `imu_bridge.py` + `test_imu_bridge.py` → 放进 `tools/servo-web/`（比如叫 `imu_jlink.py`）。这是你写的核心，原样搬过去
- `server.py` 加一个可选参数，比如 `--imu-jlink config.json`：给了就起你的 bridge 线程，姿态数据走调试台**现有的 WebSocket**（新加一种消息 `{"type": "imu", ...}`），不另开服务、不另开端口
- 日志用调试台现有的 `log(msg, cat, level)` 约定（分类可以新加一个「IMU」），这样出问题都在同一个日志文件里，能对着时间线查
- `imu.html` 里的姿态显示并进 `index.html`：3D 鸭子的**躯干**按 IMU 四元数转，关节照旧按舵机读数转。安装方向（`DEFAULT_MOUNT` 绕 Y +90°）和归零按钮保留
- 没接 J-Link 的时候这块就不显示，调试台其它功能照常

**建议先不进主仓库的**：三个 `.cmd` 启动器、`package.py`、`PACKAGE_FILES.txt`、分享 ZIP 那套。给队友打包分发的需求可以另外做，主仓库里调试台统一用 `python server.py` 启动。

## 3. 文档

- 顶层 `README.md` 和 `software/README.md` 的改动跟着新位置改：固件的说明放 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/README.md`，查看器的用法放 `tools/servo-web/README.md` 加一节
- `VALIDATION.md` 很好，建议保留在固件目录里

## 4. 合并前自检

```bash
cd tools/servo-web
python selftest.py          # 调试台自带的自检，现在 36+ 项，要全过
python -m pytest test_imu_bridge.py
```

## 下一步（不急，这次不用做）

固件协议层改成飞特那套以后（ID 200、地址 56、15 字节，规格在 [`hardware/imu_to_dxl/总线协议.md`](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/hardware/imu_to_dxl/%E6%80%BB%E7%BA%BF%E5%8D%8F%E8%AE%AE.md)），调试台就能**直接从舵机串口总线读 IMU**，不用 J-Link 了 —— J-Link 那条路留着做裸板调试。

改完用这个验收，13 项检查的判据全是照主控源码写的，过了就能上整机：

```bash
python tools/imu200/imu200.py check --port COMx
```

有问题随时问，辛苦了！

parent_context.title: How is the articulated beak/grasp modeled in simulation?
parent_context.text:
Hi! I’m looking into grasping with MicroDuck and wanted to clarify how the beak is intended to be modeled in simulation.

From the current public microduck_rl model and policy interface, I understand that the locomotion policies use 14 actuated joints and that the mouth is excluded from the policy action space. The current GroundPick behavior also appears to focus on lowering the mouth tip to the ground and returning upright, rather than simulating an articulated beak closing on an object.

A few questions:

Is there currently a physical jaw/beak joint + actuator model used internally for grasp simulation that is not yet included in this repository?
On the real robot, is beak closing during the advertised Grab behavior handled by a scripted/high-level controller outside the 14D policy?
Is physics-based grasping — articulated beak + contact/friction, without kinematic attachment/latching — planned for the public simulator?

If this functionality is currently missing, I’d be interested in implementing it in a backward-compatible way: keeping the existing 14D locomotion policies unchanged, adding an independently controlled jaw actuator, and providing a minimal contact-based grasp demo.

Would that be a contribution you’d be open to reviewing upstream?
parent_context.author: toyhank

text:
Could you share the current mouth's joint/linkage definition, or an articulated MJCF/URDF export?

For a contact-based pinch-and-lift test, the missing piece is how the two beak contact surfaces move relative to one another as the mouth command changes. The public ground-contact model merges the jaw meshes into the head body, while the runtime controls the mouth independently.

The smallest useful data would be the moving-part membership, joint pivot/axis and zero/sign, actuator-to-jaw linkage or transmission, and travel limits. Per-link masses/inertias and mouth actuator details would also help preserve the stock dynamics.

The intended integration would retain the existing 61D observations and 14 policy actions, with a separate mouth-control path matching the hardware. A small mechanism export would be sufficient; a complete robot CAD export is not necessary.

parent_context.title: Velocity-family training converges to standing-in-place across all reward/curriculum variants — full diagnostic matrix
parent_context.text:
**Title: Velocity-family training converges to standing-in-place across all reward/curriculum variants — full diagnostic matrix**

## Environment

- Repo at `29e887e` (Sep 2, includes `fix not walking` + the velocity2 merge)
- Pinned env from `uv.lock`: warp-lang 1.12.0, mujoco 3.10.0, mjlab 1.3.0, torch 2.9.1+cu128
- 4× L4 (sm_89), driver 570.172.08 (CUDA 12.8), Ubuntu, training on 4096 envs
- Tasks: `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, `Mjlab-VelStand-Flat-MicroDuck`, plus a registered RampReg variant of Velocity-Flat (see below)

## Symptom

Every velocity-family run converges to a **standing / stepping-in-place policy**:

- `Metrics/twist/error_vel_xy` plateaus at ~0.43 (command ranges lin ±0.4 / ang ±1.0, so ≈ mean |cmd|)
- Net displacement 0.1–0.6 m per 20 s episode; `Episode_Reward/air_time ≈ 0.002` (feet never leave the ground) until very late
- Reward breakdown shows `upright` (2.0) and `head_pose_tracking` (2.0) as the dominant positive mass while the robot stands

Meanwhile the **pose tasks train fine** with the same pipeline: StandUp-Flat reaches 90% envs standing within 200 steps; SitStand transitions verified (98% of envs switch posture). So the env/RL plumbing itself works.

## Diagnostic matrix (what we tried)

| # | Hypothesis | Experiment | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regularizers suppress gait exploration (AGENTS.md "attempt-tax") | Tracking-only rewards (all 11 non-tracking terms weight 0), 1500 iters | error 0.39→0.23, slow but real; still no gait; displacement <1 m |
| 2 | Same + regularizers ramped in at iter 800 (repo's `reward_weight`) | RampReg run, 5000 iters | error dips to 0.15 @1565 then rises to 0.37 — standing wins again |
| 3 | Gait bootstrap missing | air_time (3.0) + foot_swing + foot_clearance at full weight from step 0, all penalties deferred to iter 6000 | error briefly 0.10, air_time activates (0.02), late-episode displacement surge to 0.52 m — then regresses to standing by iter 11300 |
| 4 | Torque insufficiency (BAM M6 force_limit ±1.07 Nm) | vin_range (6.5,8.2)→(6.5,16.4) (force_limit ≈ ×2 via kt·V/R), tracking-only 300 iters | error 0.44 @242 vs 0.29 control — **worse**, hypothesis rejected |
| 5 | DR push_robot events corrupt displacement evals | Disabled push_robot; forced constant forward command via `obs["actor"][48:51]=(0.3,0,0)` | displacement 0.04 m / path 0.11 m over 12 s — policy genuinely does not walk |
| 6 | Official checkpoint as reference | `alpha_walking.onnx` under our sim (privileged obs) | drifts 0.66 m / 20 s — also does not walk (obs-convention mismatch suspected: sensor-view vs privileged, so inconclusive) |
| 7 | Version drift | `uv.lock`-pinned install, verified | ruled out |

Note on #5/#6: we found `push_robot` interval events (3–6 s) firing during train-mode evals — worth flagging for anyone benchmarking displacement on train-mode envs.

## Ask

Our working hypothesis is now that something differs between the HF Jobs training setup and a stock `uv.lock` local run, or that a specific seed/config detail is needed to escape the standing local optimum. Questions:

1. Has anyone hit standing-in-place convergence on the velocity tasks, and what was the escape?
2. Is there a known-good wandb run config (seed, hyperparameters, any uncommitted tweaks) for the merged velocity recipe that we should replicate exactly?
3. For `alpha_walking.onnx`: what observation view does it expect (privileged sim obs vs onboard sensor view), and what normalizer stats/ordering? (Related to #40.)

Happy to share training logs, checkpoints, the RampReg task patch, and the diagnostic scripts (`eval_skill.py`, `disp_eval.py`, `force_cmd_eval.py`).

## What works

StandUp / SitStand / (partially) VelStand-prone-reset recovery — all verified numerically with train-mode evals. The pipeline, DR stack, and eval tooling are solid; it's specifically velocity-gait discovery that never happens.
parent_context.author: ysaima

text:
A data point from the deployment side, in case it helps: the shipped walking policy shows the same thing in `duck-sim`, and it barely turns either.

Setup: macOS, `microduck` at `daemon-v0.15.0` (a9ec4b2), `microduck_rl` develop at cb70b79 for the body, `scripts/duck-sim` headless, one duck. robotd logs `policy loaded mode="walk" walk=…/policies/current/alpha_walking.onnx`.

From standing, `robot.move` at 10 Hz for 60 s (vx 0.08, vyaw −0.245), reading `robot.state` at 10 Hz:

```
t     policy  move.applied                 odom.position (x, y)   odom.yaw
0 s   stand   [0, 0, 0] (deadman)          0.0401, -0.0112        0.7912
10 s  walk    [0.08, 0.0, -0.245]          0.0399, -0.0086        0.6922
30 s  walk    [0.08, 0.0, -0.245]          0.0399, -0.0089        0.6877
60 s  walk    [0.08, 0.0, -0.245]          0.0398, -0.0090        0.6815
```

`safety.fallen` stays false throughout. So the command arrives and is applied, the duck steps, and the body moves about 2 mm in 60 s where ~4.8 m were commanded. Yaw drops 0.10 rad in the first 10 s (around the stand → walk switch) and then 0.011 rad over the next 50 s, where ~12 rad were commanded.

Adds a Modal backend for training, alongside the existing HF Jobs path. Same
contract as `--hf-jobs` — same source snapshot (tracked + uncommitted files),
same wandb forwarding, same auto-export to ONNX — but the dependency install is
baked into a cached image, so a warm start is seconds instead of minutes.

## Usage

Your normal train command, plus `--modal`:

```bash
uv run train Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck \
    --env.scene.num-envs 4096 --agent.max_iterations 6000 --modal
```

Without the flag, nothing changes. Submission flags (`--gpu`, `--timeout`,
`--detach`, `--dry-run`, `--no-wandb`, `--no-export`, …) are consumed locally;
everything else is forwarded verbatim to `uv run train` in the container.
`scripts/modal/README.md` has the full set.

## How it works

`train_hook.py` previously hardcoded the one `--hf-jobs` flag. It now dispatches
a table, still intercepted from the `mjlab.tasks` plugin entry point before tyro
parses argv:

```
--hf-jobs  -> mjlab_microduck.hf_jobs
--modal    -> mjlab_microduck.modal_jobs
```

Each submitter module exposes `submit(argv) -> int` and receives argv minus the
flag, so adding a third backend is a table entry. `scripts/modal/train_modal.py`
is a shim that calls `submit()` directly, matching the HF path's escape hatch.

Image is `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu22.04` + python 3.12 + uv, with
`uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project` cached until `pyproject.toml` /
`uv.lock` change. A Modal Volume `microduck-rl-logs` is mounted at `/work/logs`
and committed every 60 s, so checkpoints survive a timeout or a crash. The wandb
key travels as a per-run Secret (read from `$WANDB_API_KEY` or `~/.netrc`), so it
is not baked into the image.

## Notes

- Log/stop hints print the Modal **app id**, not the app name: training apps are
  ephemeral, and `modal app logs <name>` resolves names only for *deployed* apps
  (it errors with "No App with name ... found"). `scripts/modal/README.md` says
  the same.
- `modal>=1.0` is in a `[dependency-groups] dev` group, so it is not pulled into
  the container (`uv sync --no-dev`).

## Testing

`tests/test_modal_jobs.py` (8 tests) covers flag interception, argv forwarding,
and the submission spec; `tests/test_hf_jobs_flag.py` still passes unchanged, so
the refactor doesn't disturb the HF path. 20 passed locally.

End to end: a 6000-iteration `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck` run at 4096 envs on
an L4 finished in 5h09m, exit 0, mean reward 119.4, with checkpoints in wandb and
`exported/policy.onnx` written to the volume.

Updates `tailwind-merge` from 3.6.0 to 3.7.0
Release notes

Sourced from tailwind-merge's releases.

tailwind-merge@3.7.0

New Features

  • Prepare some upcoming changes by @​dcastil in dcastil/tailwind-merge#713
    • Theme getters returned by fromTheme now expose the theme key they read as a themeKey property, so tooling can identify the referenced theme scale without calling the getter.
    • Release tags now include the package name, starting with tailwind-merge@3.7.0.

Bug Fixes

  • Fix arbitrary values using color() or light-dark() being classified as lengths instead of colors by @​ddussi in dcastil/tailwind-merge#712
  • Fix bare bg-conic not merging with other background image classes by @​dcastil in dcastil/tailwind-merge#708
  • Fix columns-auto not conflicting with other columns classes by @​dcastil in dcastil/tailwind-merge#707
  • Fix container sizes like inline-2xl not merging by @​dcastil in dcastil/tailwind-merge#706
  • Fix max-h-none missing in max-h class group by @​mutewinter in dcastil/tailwind-merge#704
  • Fix axis shorthands like px not overriding logical sides like ps by @​dcastil in dcastil/tailwind-merge#705
  • Fix leading-none being removed when the leading theme scale is overridden by @​chatman-media in dcastil/tailwind-merge#689
  • Fix deprecated shadow-inner being classified as shadow color instead of shadow by @​dcastil in dcastil/tailwind-merge#703

Documentation

  • Add Deno to install instructions by @​bartlomieju in dcastil/tailwind-merge#687
  • Add missing text-shadow theme key to configuration docs by @​dcastil in https://github.com/dcastil/tailwind-merge/commit/3e6d2080a9905b5cc55f4b1515450544e761ded7

Other

  • Switch package manager from yarn to pnpm by @​dcastil in dcastil/tailwind-merge#680
  • Harden CI security by @​dcastil in dcastil/tailwind-merge#679

parent_context.title: Add play-dead task: stand, flop onto the back, and hold
parent_context.text:
## Why

Sit is a polite sit. Roulade lands on its feet. Standup starts already down. Nothing in the pad means **die and stay dead** — swap the ONNX in, the duck goes down and holds; swap sitstand/standup to revive.

Play-dead is **supine** (belly up, −90° pitch), not “inverted”. `upright_cos = −1` is a headstand **and** a face-plant; a policy will farm whichever is cheaper. The orientation signal is world-z of body +X (`body_supine_cos_from_quat`). Height rewards are gated on `supine_cos > 0` so sitting (`z ≈ 0.060`) cannot collect the dead-height peak.

## What

- New env family `Mjlab-PlayDead-{Flat,Rough}-MicroDuck` (+ backlash twins on the allcollisions model)
- 61D actor obs: 48 proprio + twist(3) + head(4) pad + body(6) pad — hot-swappable with walk/stand/roulade
- Reset mix: 75% standing (learn the flop) / 25% already face-up (learn the hold); reverse curriculum raises the dead fraction; face-down stays at 0
- `scripts/infer_policy.py --playdead` (key **D**). Default is hold-until-D-again — play-dead does not end standing
- CPU cfg tests lock the contract, signs, sit-basin audit, and registration

## AGENTS.md bar

```bash
uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_playdead_cfg.py
uv run train Mjlab-PlayDead-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5
```

Ran on a Spark (GB10): 16 play-dead tests + full CPU suite (171) green. Smoke 64 envs × 5 iters: actor obs **(61,)**, every reward term computed, `Episode_Termination/nan_state = 0`, self-negating penalties logged **≤ 0**, ONNX export **61 → 14**.

This is the env, not a converged policy. A real run is `~1000–2000` iters at 4096 envs (`experiment_name=microduck_playdead`), then `scripts/export.py` (bakes the normalizer — mandatory).

## Deploy rehearsal

```bash
uv run scripts/infer_policy.py --walking walk.onnx --standing stand.onnx \
    --playdead playdead.onnx --new-cmd-obs
```

`D` plays dead and holds; `D` again hands back. Revive with standup/sitstand, not walk.

parent_context.title: fix(hf-jobs): auto-export never finds the checkpoint
parent_context.text:
The auto-export step at the end of a HF Jobs run never fires: it reports
`[bootstrap] no checkpoint found, skipping auto-export` even though the uploader
has just pushed several `model_*.pt` files from the very same run.

Two bugs, one behind the other:

1. **The glob is one level too shallow.** `rsl_rl` writes to
   `logs/rsl_rl/<experiment_name>/<timestamp>_<run_name>/model_*.pt`, but the
   bootstrap looks for `logs/rsl_rl/*/model_*.pt`, which matches nothing.

2. **The checkpoint is passed by basename.** `scripts/export.py` does
   `Path(cfg.checkpoint_file)` and then `.exists()`, resolved relative to the
   working directory (`/work`), so a bare `model_19.pt` fails even once found.

This matters more than a missing convenience: `scripts/export.py` builds an mjlab
env and therefore needs CUDA. A user with no local GPU — the exact audience
`--hf-jobs` exists for — cannot export the checkpoint afterwards. The run
completes, uploads its `.pt` files, and leaves nothing deployable behind.

Verified on two jobs, `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, 1024 envs, 20 iterations,
flavor `l4x1`:

- before: `[bootstrap] no checkpoint found, skipping auto-export`
- after: `[bootstrap] auto-exporting ONNX from model_19.pt` → `Written /work/policy.onnx` → `[bootstrap] uploaded exported/policy.onnx`

parent_context.title: Walking policy won't start slow walk from stand still
parent_context.text:
Hi! I've been setting up `duck-sim` and noticed the duck wouldn't walk when I asked for a slow walk. It just stands there. I dug in a bit and I think it's the shipped v5 policies rather than anything in the runtime.

From a standstill, both `alpha_walking.onnx` and `velstand.onnx` refuse to take a step below about 0.22 m/s, even though training samples `lin_vel_x` from `(-0.4, 0.4)`. What surprised me is that it happens in the training env too. I ran the ONNX in `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck` with a pinned twist command (32 envs, mean forward speed in m/s):

| cmd vx | play cfg as is | play cfg, pushes off | `velstand`, pushes off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.15 | 0.078 | **0.007** (1/32 walking) | **0.002** (0/32) |
| 0.20 | – | 0.071 (10/32) | 0.021 (1/32) |
| 0.30 | 0.146 | 0.144 | 0.141 |

I think the reason nobody's caught it is that in-sim play pushes the robot every 0.5–1.0 s, and each push nudges it into stepping. So in play it looks fine. Once it's moving it'll happily keep going at 0.15. It just can't *start* slow. I see the same thing in `scripts/infer_policy.py` and through `robotd --sim`, so it doesn't look like a sim2sim gap.

It feels related to #46, but this one is about the policies people are running right now.

A few ideas, in case they're useful:

- **Evaluate with pushes off.** The export/publish check, or a quick play mode, could command a slow speed from rest with pushes disabled, so this shows up before a set ships.
- **Look at the forward-only share.** The base cfg has `rel_forward_envs=0.2` with forward-only commands clamped to `vx >= 0.3`, so a chunk of training never sees slow forward walking. I haven't verified this is the cause, though.
- **More episodes starting at rest.** Episodes that begin from a standstill with a small nonzero command would teach it to break into a walk at low speed.


Tested on `develop` @ `cb70b79`, `seed-v5`

Speeds are means measured from the simulator's ground truth, ramp included, in the trunk's starting heading.
